fix(bounds): respect disablePadding and explicit position props in bounds calculation

Bounds calculation now honours the disablePadding flag (locks content
when it fits the wrapper) and applies minPositionX/maxPositionX/
minPositionY/maxPositionY prop overrides. Pinch and wheel handlers
enforce these explicit bounds via hasExplicitPositionBounds. Initial
state creation clamps scale to minScale/maxScale and respects position
bounds.

Also includes:
- src/ added to published package files for source maps
- ResizeObserver mock in jest.setup for centerOnInit flows
- Test assertions updated for synchronous setTransform calls and
  correct pan directions
- Storybook enhanced with bounds overlay, cinema venue example, and
  mixed-content demos

Made-with: Cursor

fix(zoom): remove setState rounding that caused trackpad pinch-to-zoom drift

setState was rounding scale to 2 decimal places and position to 3 decimal
places via parseFloat(toFixed(N)). During rapid trackpad pinch-to-zoom
(many small sequential wheel events), this quantization compounded
frame-over-frame, causing the zoom center to visibly tremble and drift.

Also removes stale hasExplicitPositionBounds reference from wheel.logic
(already deleted from bounds.utils).

Made-with: Cursor

fix(pan): handle stale mouse/keyboard state across iframe boundaries

When the library runs inside an iframe, mouseup and keyup events fired
in the parent frame never reach the iframe listeners, causing pan jumps
and stuck activation keys.

- Detect missed mouseup by checking event.buttons === 0 on mousemove
- Clear pressedKeys and isPanning on window blur
- Sync modifier keys (Ctrl, Meta, Shift, Alt) from mouse/wheel events
  so activation keys work without requiring focus/keydown
- Scale explicit position bounds (minPositionX, etc.) with zoom level
  so the same content-space region stays reachable at every scale

Updates all test mouse events to include the buttons property matching
real browser behavior, adds iframe and bounds-scaling regression tests,
and improves the cinema story with a seat map widget.

Made-with: Cursor

fix(pan): use content-overflow check instead of scale > 1 for velocity

The velocity guards (isVelocityCalculationAllowed, isVelocityAllowed,
handlePanningEnd) incorrectly gated on `scale > 1`, preventing inertia
for natively large content at default zoom. Replaced with an actual
content-vs-wrapper overflow check using offsetWidth/offsetHeight.

Also fixed a click-after-zoom snap bug where tiny mouse jitter (<=5px)
during a click would trigger velocity panning, flinging the viewport.
A minimum displacement threshold now distinguishes clicks from real pans.

Additional changes:
- Round scale in CSS transform to strip binary float noise
- Fix incorrect || logic in isVelocityAllowed (should be &&)
- Refactor storybook Controls with icon buttons and glassmorphism UI
- Fix pinch direction in test utility
- Expand and simplify test suites

Closes #363

refactor(core-test): pass modifier keys via event properties instead of keyDown

Test helpers now propagate ctrlKey/shiftKey/etc. through synthesized
mouse and wheel events rather than dispatching separate keyDown events.
This mirrors how syncModifierKeys reads modifier state from interaction
events, making tests more realistic—especially for iframe scenarios
where keydown never fires.

Made-with: Cursor

fix(pan): sync modifier key release via event flags in iframes

syncModifierKeys now writes both true and false states from event
modifier flags instead of only setting keys to true. This prevents
stale pressed-key state when keyup never fires (e.g. unfocused iframe).

Also passes the actual clamped scale from this.state.scale to the
onTransform callback instead of the pre-clamp local variable.

Made-with: Cursor

fix(test): pass modifier flags on WheelEvent for activationKeys tests

for iframe support), so fireEvent.keyDown alone is insufficient — the
subsequent WheelEvent must carry the modifier flag just like a real
browser would. Also adds a positive assertion for the predicate-based
activationKeys test.

fix(zoom): prevent NaN propagation from invalid mouse/touch positions (#566)

* fix(zoom): prevent NaN propagation from invalid mouse positions

getMousePosition logs the error but still returned NaN coordinates,
which flowed into setState and triggered 'Detected NaN set state values'.
Return a safe {x:0,y:0} fallback instead.

handleCalculateZoomPositions guarded with `typeof !== 'number'`, which
passes for NaN since typeof NaN === 'number'. Switch to Number.isFinite
so NaN and Infinity are also caught and the current position is returned.

These two bugs combine: if scale reaches a degenerate state and
event.clientX === contentRect.left, the division 0/0 produces NaN which
bypassed the type guard and corrupted transform state.

* test(regression): add NaN mouse position guard tests (#566)

Unit tests for getMousePosition (returns safe fallback on NaN) and
handleCalculateZoomPositions (Number.isFinite guard catches NaN/Infinity).
Integration test confirms wheel events with NaN bounding rect cannot
corrupt transform state.

fix(pan): keep form controls, contenteditable and draggable subtrees out of panning

Inputs, textareas, selects and anything nested inside a contenteditable
or draggable element no longer start a pan or cancel mousedown/touchstart,
so native editing and HTML5 drag keep working. Double-click on editable
targets no longer zooms (word selection wins). Previously only the element
carrying the attribute itself was skipped, never its children, and form
controls were not covered at all.

Closes #437
Closes #544
Closes #460

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(wheel): stop horizontal swipes zooming out and clamp trackpad pans to live bounds

A wheel event with deltaY 0 (Magic Mouse or trackpad horizontal swipe) was
read as a zoom-out step; it now carries no zoom intent and, with
trackPadPanning enabled, pans horizontally instead. Trackpad panning also
computed its bounds only at mount, so after any zoom it clamped against
the wrong range; bounds are recalculated when a trackpad pan starts, the
same way a mouse pan does.

Closes #168
Closes #396
Closes #433

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(zoom): make zoomIn, zoomOut and double-click step an absolute increment

Under the default smooth: true the button and double-click step was
applied exponentially (zoomIn(0.25) from 1 landed on 1.284, zoomIn(0.5)
on 1.649). step now adds to the scale as documented; smooth keeps
shaping wheel and trackpad deltas only.

BREAKING-ish for callers relying on the exponential feel: default
double-click now zooms from 1 to 1.7 instead of 2.01.

Closes #545
Closes #431

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(minimap): stop leaking a document mousedown listener on every render

The drag effect re-registered its mousedown handler each render and never
removed it, so one drag ran N handlers after N renders. Listeners are now
scoped to the mini map's own document and fully removed on cleanup; the
unused mirror instance ref is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(core): clean up on unmount and initialize before the first paint

The mounted flag never turned false, so wheel, double-click and zoom-stop
timers, animation frames and callbacks kept running against a detached
tree. TransformWrapper now unmounts the instance, timers and wrapper
listeners are cleared, animation frames are cancelled by handle (a
replaced animation no longer re-schedules its successor twice per frame or
applies a stale final step), and everything is StrictMode-safe.

Initialization moved to a layout effect so centerOnInit, initial
positions and virtualized children are right before the browser paints;
Virtualize computes visibility on its first render, which removes the
one-frame flash the whiteboard integration had to work around.

Also: KeepScale applies its counter-scale on mount, zoomToElement(id)
resolves in the wrapper's own document, a third quick tap no longer
counts as a second double tap, prop updates recalculate bounds from the
new setup, and instances are created lazily instead of once per render.

Closes #516
Ref #483
Ref #392
Ref #290

fix(wheel): apply wheel events that arrive during the alignment window

handleWheelStop schedules the auto-alignment after 100 ms while the stop timer
runs for 160 ms; handleWheelStart only cancelled animations when the stop
timer was idle, so a wheel event landing in that window had its setState
overwritten by the alignment's next frame. Cancel on every wheel event and
skip alignment animations whose target equals the current state.

Closes #582

fix(build): ship source maps that resolve and embed their sources

The published maps listed sources as ../../src/x.ts, one level too deep for a
map in dist/, so bundlers looked for node_modules/src/x.ts. They also had an
empty sourcesContent for every TypeScript file, which is why bundlers needed
the path at all. Rollup now rewrites the paths to ../src/ and a small plugin
embeds the source text; the build fails if a source cannot be read.

The regression spec verifies every source of both built maps has content and
that src paths resolve, instead of only checking the files field.

Closes #529, closes #542
